channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Evacuation from Oleshky: How are preparations going?
item.description: A lawyer with the Save Ukraine Foundation, Myroslava Kharchenko, told DW about what has been happening in Russian-occupied Oleshky since a temporary ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump took effect.

item.title: [DW] EU's 'Made in Europe' push unnerves global auto suppliers
item.description: In shielding Europe's carmakers from Chinese rivals, the EU risks hurting close partners from Turkey and Morocco to Japan and South Korea. Billions in trade and hundreds of thousands of European jobs are at stake.

item.title: [DW] Russia in Africa: What is Putin hoping to achieve?
item.description: Following its invasion of Ukraine and the resulting rift with the West, Russia has declared that it intends to make a "historic return" to Africa. What have we seen of this so far?

item.title: [DW] Serbian police shoot dead assailant at Israeli Embassy
item.description: A "minor" has been killed by police after attacking a guard at Israel's embassy in Belgrade with knives, the interior minister says. Ivica Dacic said police had declared the highest terror alert after the incident.

item.title: [DW] Cyprus: From ties with Russia to a strategic alignment with the US
item.description: The Republic of Cyprus long balanced ties between Russia and the West. Now, it is phasing out Russian weapons, expanding defense cooperation with the United States and redefining its place in the Eastern Mediterranean.

item.title: [DW] Could the AI boom make borrowing more expensive in Europe?
item.description: France, Germany and Italy face a volatile bond market as war inflation bites. With US tech giants now issuing billions in AI bonds, they are competing with cash-strapped European governments.

item.description: Prime Minister Tusk says overhaul of Constitutional Tribunal is vital to preserve EU-aligned rule of law, while President Nawrocki accuses him of a coup.

item.description: Cary is just a small town in North Carolina. But it is also part of a larger campaign by the Democrats to take over the Senate during this mid-term election.

item.description: Microsoft hosts key software used to monitor movements of Palestinians in the occupied West bank. Some of this is being hosted in Ireland.

item.title: [EU Observer] Serbia’s Student List has been inspirational, but the big test will be forming a stable anti-corruption government
item.description: The Serbian campaign looked exceptional. I cannot think of many cases of an opposition that was so decentralised and so democratic internally. The closest comparison may be the early German Greens that had a strong Basisdemokratie ["Grassroots Democracy"] out of conviction; or the faceless and fluid democratic movement in Hong Kong ("Be Water") out of necessity. This is inspirational.

item.title: [Euractiv] Not just another parcel: EU customs should recognise second-hand [Promoted Content]
item.description: Since 1 November, EU e-commerce imports face a €2 handling fee on top of a €3 flat duty. Nine out of 10 second-hand goods imported into the EU via eBay travel in small parcels. Customs should distinguish new from used.

item.description: The opposition has already called for snap elections

item.title: [EU Observer] Merz, Meloni and the EU: How political attacks on rescue charities are leaving migrants to drown
item.description: Berlin, Rome and Brussels have played a role in the decline in an increasingly vital force in the Mediterranean. Search-and-rescue ships have been hampered by legal hurdles and funding cuts, while the central Mediterranean has become a grave for tens of thousands of people.

item.description: Polling for POLITICO by PF Global finds the U.K. public believes a Republican victory would be riskier for the world.

item.title: [EU Observer] When adults take over youth protests, EU children’s own demands vanish
item.description: As youth protests spread from France to Belgium, Spain, Italy, Greece and Albania, Europe is confronting a stark test of whether under‑18s are treated as political actors in their own right, or merely as props in adult power struggles.

item.title: [Politico Europe] EU to host Ukraine reconstruction talks with US and UK
item.description: France, Germany, the U.K., NATO and the World Bank will join representatives from Washington, Kyiv and the EU in Brussels.

item.title: [Financial Times] What 21 months of Trump have done to America
item.description: From ‘liberation day’ and bond market turmoil to Maduro’s capture, the goading of Zelenskyy and war in Iran, it has been a head-spinning period in US politics

item.title: [EU Observer] Czech MEP Markéta Gregorová stopped at Chinese border in ‘pseudo-scare tactics’
item.description: MEP Markéta Gregorová claims to have been stopped in Beijing in what she called “pseudo-scare tactics” over the arrest of a Chinese national accused of spying in Czech Republic.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: What’s at stake for Europe in the US midterms?
item.description: Americans are voting today in the midterm elections. All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are up for grabs, along with a third of the Senate and according to the polls, the Republicans are expected to lose seats.

item.title: [EU Observer] Andrew Tate’s toxic legacy in Romania is warping its democracy
item.description: While prosecutors chase the Tates across borders, their macho fantasy of domination is already shaping how a frustrated generation of Romanian men sees women and democracy itself.

item.title: [Politico Europe] Eurozone countries to nominate Lagarde replacement by Nov. 6
item.description: Eurozone finance ministers will discuss the candidates at their gathering next Monday.

item.title: [EU Observer] Frontex drones helped Libya and Tunisia forcibly return at least 33,000 people in the central Mediterranean
item.description: The EU's border agency Frontex is instrumental in helping Libya and Tunisia intercept migrants in distress. A new study reveals the extent of those Frontex-assisted interceptions, totalling some 33,000 between 2018 and 2024.

item.title: [DW] European Central Bank (ECB) head Christine Lagarde to step down in February, before her term ends
item.description: European Central Bank (ECB) President Christine Lagarde is to resign nine months ahead of the end of her 8-year term. European Council President Antonio Costa has said the process to find a successor is underway.

item.title: [DW] France: Hundreds arrested after nationwide protests
item.description: The French government says more than 1,000 people were arrested following nationwide protests on Saturday. Police and elite security forces were out in force across the country as clashes broke out.

item.title: [DW] Russia's giant new radar in Kaliningrad raises alarm in NATO
item.description: Russia is nearing completion of what experts think is a giant radar complex in Kaliningrad, capable of monitoring much of Europe. Experts warn the project could intensify the military standoff between Moscow and NATO.

item.title: [DW] Ethnic Germans in Kazakhstan face legacy of the Soviet Union
item.description: Kazakhstan is struggling to deal with the legacy of the Soviet dictatorship. Some 85 years ago, Stalin deported hundreds of thousands of people: Some 400,000 ethnic Germans living in the USSR were sent to Kazakhstan.

item.title: [DW] Serbia after Vucic: The winners are losing patience
item.description: After the Student List's election victory, Aleksandar Vucic's power apparatus is disintegrating. People want justice as soon as possible. But the losers still hold sway in the judiciary and administration.

item.title: [DW] Global pedestrian Karl Bushby returns home to UK after 28-year trek
item.description: Karl Bushby, a British man who traveled 50,000 km without transport over the past 28 years, has come home. Starting in Chile, he crossed the Americas, Russia and parts of Central Asia and Europe — almost all on foot.

item.title: [DW] How Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria
item.description: Iliana Yotova won the presidential election in Bulgaria, promising to be a "president of peace." But the campaign showed how divided Bulgarians are about the war in Ukraine and drone attacks in the Black Sea.

item.title: [Financial Times] ‘A massive piece of pool’: Trump talks algae and grass in final midterm push
item.description: US President touts new pipes and ‘great reflectivity’ of Washington’s Reflecting Pool on eve of critical vote

item.title: [EU Observer] Whisper it, but the UK’s path back to the EU is beginning to take shape
item.description: Kaja Kallas and Wes Streeting set the scene for a process of improving EU-UK relations on Monday. Their logical conclusion is the UK rejoining, some day.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Explainer] Polish right turns court dispute into election battleground, dragging in the EU
item.description: A fight over Poland’s top court is fuelling tensions ahead of next year’s election, with judicial independence, EU relations and the country’s future in the bloc all caught up in the dispute.

item.title: [DW] Canadian PM Mark Carney discusses talks with the EU, overdependence on the US and how to deal with Donald Trump in a DW interview.
item.description: Prime Minister Mark Carney tells DW that Canada is seeking closer EU ties to "diversify and deepen" partnerships beyond the Americas. Despite German pushback, he said he favors the all-new term "associate membership."

item.title: [DW] What the rift within the Tsikhanouski family means for the Belarusian opposition in exile
item.description: Siarhei Tsikhanouski criticizes the work of his wife, Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya, and her office. He also questions her legitimacy. What are the implications for Belarusian political forces in exile?
